## Biological Interpretation

The enrichment analysis reveals that the differentially abundant metabolites map predominantly to pathways involved in **Biological oxidations**, consistent with a broad perturbation of xenobiotic metabolism in response to the treatment.

**Key driver compounds.** Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (BaP-DHD-oxide, KEGG C14853) and beta-mercaptoethanol (C00928) are confirmed members of the **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** pathway (R-HSA-156580). BaP-DHD-oxide is the ultimate carcinogenic bioactivation product of benzo[a]pyrene metabolism and a classic substrate for GST-mediated conjugation, which sequesters it into water-soluble mercapturic acid derivatives for elimination. Beta-mercaptoethanol is also annotated to this pathway, consistent with heightened demand for reduced sulphur pools during electrophilic detoxification. N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319) is confirmed as a member of **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** and is additionally annotated to **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (R-HSA-211945), reflecting its dual roles as both a Phase I oxidation product and a Phase II conjugation substrate.

**Phase I oxidation.** Coumarin (C05851) and methimazole (C07190) are both confirmed members of **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (R-HSA-211945), consistent with their known roles as substrates or modulators of cytochrome P450 and flavin-containing monooxygenase enzymes. Both are additionally annotated to **Biological oxidations** (R-HSA-211859). Glutathione (C00051) is a confirmed member of **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** (R-HSA-156580).

**Biological significance.** The metabolites collectively define a detoxification response centred on the **Biological oxidations** pathway. BaP-DHD-oxide, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, coumarin and methimazole occupy Phase I reactions, while BaP-DHD-oxide, beta-mercaptoethanol and glutathione participate in downstream Phase II conjugation. Pantothenic acid (C00864) maps to **Coenzyme A biosynthesis** (R-HSA-196783) and provides ancillary metabolic context separate from the xenobiotic response.

**Verified directional relationship.** BaP-DHD-oxide (C14853) is confirmed in both **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** and **Glutathione conjugation** (R-HSA-156590), placing it at the interface between Phase I bioactivation and Phase II detoxication in the sequential xenobiotic-metabolising cascade.

---

**Limitations.** Mechanistic details regarding GST-catalysed conjugation and methimazole's peroxidase-inhibitory activity rely on general biochemical knowledge and would require enzyme-activity data to confirm within this dataset.
